meta.compiler: STCL ledger pass, AI-assisted under human direction
meta.coverage_note: Independently verified (2026-06-06): three blind verifier agents re-fetched the official ISED source and re-derived every quote; one initially-disputed claim was adjudicated and confirmed via a targeted re-read. All 39 factual claims source-matched; 0 open. Categories: corroborated (source + an outside source), per the source, qualified by the source (the government's own hedges, estimates, and one self-contradiction), recomputed (our totals/counts), our analysis (editorial lenses). Labels are reproducible via confidence-rubric.md.

post_launch.note: Claims with ids starting 'post:' record announcements made after the strategy's June 2026 publication. They were read from official pages on 2026-10-23, then independently re-read the same day by three blind verifier agents (briefed with the claim and the URL only, not our quotes or labels, and told to try to refute). Five were confirmed as worded and five with qualifications that were folded into the wording; one (post:dtc-launch) was disputed, reworded and re-confirmed. Human sign-off is still pending. They are shown separately in the Verification tab and never feed the headline totals.

claims.claim: Funded vs. unfunded is defined by a named dollar figure
claims.rule: A commitment is 'funded' only if the strategy attaches a named dollar figure to it; otherwise it is 'unfunded' (even if money may flow later). Applied to every commitment.

checks.note: Rule is written, applied consistently, reversible by the reader.

claims.notes: Our lens, not the government's framing.

claims.claim: Soft commitments are flagged by the source's own hedging language
claims.rule: A commitment is 'soft' where the source's own wording qualifies it ('where appropriate', 'at times', 'explore', 'assess', 'review') or labels a number 'proposed'/'estimated'. Found by searching the source for these markers, then reading each in context.
claims.notes: A hedge isn't automatically a dodge, but it's worth seeing. Each soft claim quotes its giveaway phrase.

claims.claim: New vs. leveraged money are shown distinctly
claims.rule: 'New' = money the strategy introduces; 'leveraged' = existing or previously-announced funds (mostly Budget 2025 and ongoing programs) counted toward the total. Each line-item flagged as one or the other.
claims.notes: Different kinds of commitment; kept separate so totals are honest.

claims.claim: Unfunded items are grouped into six author-defined categories
claims.rule: Unpriced commitments grouped into six categories chosen by us — Law & rights, Standards & trust, Skills & people, Market & structural, Infrastructure & sovereignty, Diplomacy & alliances — not the government's taxonomy.
claims.notes: Our groupings, stated so they can be disputed.

claims.claim: Each program is mapped to the audiences it touches
claims.rule: Each program is tagged with the personas (SME owner, founder, student, mid-career worker, researcher, creator, Indigenous communities, public servant) it materially serves. Our reading of relevance, not a mapping the source provides.
claims.notes: Drives the 'By audience' tab.

claims.claim: Eight 'gap -> response' pairings frame the programs as answers to diagnosed gaps
claims.rule: Eight clusters of programs are each framed as a response to a diagnosed gap (adoption, literacy/trust, startup exodus, sovereignty exposure, talent squeeze, harms, data silos, platform dependence). The pairing is our analytical framing; the underlying gap statistics are separate direct claims.
claims.notes: The gap statistics inside each pairing are direct claims graded separately.

claims.claim: AI Sovereign Compute Infrastructure Program: about $890M over seven fiscal years to build and operate the system; applications closed Jun 1, 2026

source.doc: ISED program page (AI Sovereign Compute Infrastructure Program)
source.quote: The program will provide approximately $890 million to the Infrastructure Build Layer to support the design, construction, and ongoing operation of the compute system, over seven fiscal years, beginning in fiscal year 2026–27 … All funding amounts are notional and are subject to negotiation.

checks.note: Read from the official page text.

checks.by: ai:source-match (second read, same session; not independent)

checks.note: Confirmed. The page says 'approximately $890 million' and that amounts are 'notional and are subject to negotiation'. Scope is build plus ongoing operation, so the claim now says 'build and operate'.

claims.notes: OPEN QUESTION (flagged, not resolved): the strategy gives the public supercomputer no dollar figure, so it stays in the Unfunded count. The strategy does not name this program; linking them is our reading (same type of system, same period). No selected proponent announced as of 2026-10-23. The $890M goes to the 'Infrastructure Build Layer' (design, construction and ongoing operation) and is contingent on Parliament and Treasury Board approvals.
